rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif Lām Rā names the sūra and introduces the demonstrative; the isolated letters were discussed at the start of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: They form the isolated letters which have been comprehensively discussed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book’s wisdom means its contents argue every claim it makes, so sound readers should inspect it rather than seek external proof.
rows.anchor: the attribute “wise” for the book points to the fact that such are arguments found within it for every claim it makes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contextual indications, “people” in the objection are the Quraysh.
rows.anchor: As per concomitant indications, the word “people” refers to the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation to a man known to the Quraysh is a favor: they know his upright character, so their own conscience witnesses to the truth.
rows.anchor: their own conscience has delivered the truth to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human messenger can serve as a model for human beings; an angel or jinn would be unsuitable.
rows.anchor: if an angel or jinn had been appointed for this task, this too would have been inappropriate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book gives explicit glad tidings of return to God and reward for believers, while leaving the warning about rejecters vague.
rows.anchor: the glad tidings found in this verse for the believers are found in clear words but the element of warning has been left vague

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam sidq suggests depth, stability, and permanence, hence an honorable place, high rank, or everlasting success.
rows.anchor: connotes depth, stability and permanence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glad tidings for believers are the chapter’s main emphasis, so the fate of disbelievers appears secondarily.
rows.anchor: the prominent element in this whole chapter is that of glad tidings for the believers. The fate of the disbelievers is mentioned secondarily in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the messenger an expert magician expresses rejection while admitting the book’s force and eloquence, which the disbelievers recast as verbal trickery.
rows.anchor: they regard its bearer to be a plain magician

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers call messengers magicians to diminish their miracles and the stature of their books, warning upright listeners away from their influence.
rows.anchor: it is not merely to lessen the importance of the miracles worked by them, it is also to lessen the stature of the book they present

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They portray the Qur’an and Prophet as ordinary sorcerers or soothsayers, likening their eloquence and predictions to familiar rhymed prose to deny divine status.
rows.anchor: just as their own soothsayers would compose rhymed prose in an embellished way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse supplies arguments for the warnings and glad tidings stated earlier.
rows.anchor: This verse presents the arguments in favour of the warnings and glad tidings stated in the previous verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the acknowledged Creator is also the Quraysh’s Lord and Master, expecting other lords is foolish and contradicts their own premises.
rows.anchor: to be the Creator is their Lord and Master as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation in six gradual phases shows a deliberate, meaningful universe rather than accident or amusement; human vicegerency therefore entails accountability, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: This gradual development and evolution itself bears witness that neither is its creation an accidental happening nor is it made as an amusement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God remains actively governing the world after creation; He did not become a silent first cause or hand its affairs to others.
rows.anchor: after creating the world, God became unconcerned with it, becoming a silent first cause and then handed over its affairs to others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession without God’s permission cannot save anyone from punishment or turn truth into falsehood, since God knows everything.
rows.anchor: none should be under the misconception that he will be able to save himself from God’s punishment through someone’s intercession

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “Do you not think?” challenges idolaters to trace their fabricated deities’ origin and notice their inconsistency with their own premises.
rows.anchor: amazingly refer to the origin of the deities the idolaters have fabricated: where have they come from?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone will return to God, including the idolaters’ deities; the word “all” stresses that none can escape this certain fate.
rows.anchor: even their deities will return to God. None will be able to evade this fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is not difficult for God because He has already originated creation once.
rows.anchor: how can it be difficult for God to create a second time when He already did this the first time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment’s real purpose is just reward for faithful people who did good; punishment of disbelievers follows naturally, restating the opening glad tidings after their proof.
rows.anchor: state the real purpose for the arrival of Judgement Day. Punishment of disbelievers is a natural consequence of it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boiling water is the first punishment disbelievers encounter, followed by harsher punishments.
rows.anchor: Boiling water will be the first thing they will encounter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe’s ordered power and mercy, including the sun’s regular course and the moon’s phases, support the case for accountability between good and evil.
rows.anchor: The sun rises at prescribed times and lights up the whole world with its radiance

rows.speaker: Some people
rows.claim: Some interpret the sun’s radiance and the moon’s light as indicating that the sun has its own light while the moon receives sunlight.
rows.anchor: Some people say that this choice of words in accordance with the fact that the sun has its own light and moon obtains its light from the sun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although that interpretation is true, Islahi says the wording primarily distinguishes warm, heat-bearing sunlight from the moon’s cool light.
rows.anchor: in my opinion the former actually refers to light that has heat in it and the latter to light which is coldish

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting accountability would make the universe’s evident power and wisdom purposeless; its grandeur makes that inference as illogical as calling great buildings purposeless.
rows.anchor: Such is the illogical, unfair and untenable nature of this inference that no upright and logical person can for a moment accept it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True human nature recognizes that creation has purpose: the world culminates in justice, judgment between truth and falsehood, and recompense for deeds.
rows.anchor: The purpose referred to is that this world reaches a culmination in which justice is meted out

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs and proofs of reward and punishment are scattered through the universe, and God explains them for people who seek understanding; Islahi points to reflection in 3:191.
rows.anchor: those who keep reflecting on the creation of the heavens and the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day and night serve different needs, and their harmonious alternation under one powerful governor points to providence and a coming judgment that rewards those who honor its claims and punishes the indifferent.
rows.anchor: the day provides people the opportunities to earn their livelihood and the night gives them rest and sleep
